notes: Read both targets and full context. Resolve pandemic, country, Walter Wallace and these needs. Preserve might-have counterfactual modality, reinvestment/divestment, the politicians' claimed working-class concern, and immediate priority for Black and Brown communities without denying benefits to everyone. Context-only firing and abolition demands are not new targets.

claims.claim_text: Support for a thorough political and social revolution in the United States to address state-sponsored violence and secure equal regard for Black and Brown lives.
The U.S. working class is suffering severely during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Black and Brown U.S. working-class communities have been devastated by COVID-19.
At the time of DSA's statement on Walter Wallace's killing, hundreds of thousands of lives have been lost to COVID-19 and police violence.
Support for policies such as the Breathe Act that reinvest in Black and Brown communities and divest from policing.
Had the Breathe Act been in place, Walter Wallace might have received appropriate care instead of being killed by police.
Access to quality health care is a human right.
Politicians claiming to care about the U.S. working class should support the Emergency Health Guarantee Act and Medicare for All.
Politicians claiming to care about the U.S. working class should reopen and rebuild hospitals.
Politicians claiming to care about the U.S. working class should fully restore public schools.
Politicians claiming to care about the U.S. working class should guarantee good jobs, safe working conditions and the ability to organize.
The health, education and employment policies sought from politicians claiming to care about the U.S. working class should begin immediately with Black and Brown working-class communities nationwide.

Health care, hospitals, public schools, good jobs, workplace safety and organizing rights benefit everyone and are essential to the well-being, preservation and liberation of Black and Brown communities.
